From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>

Subject: Pilot pricing proposal & one-time rebate (Q4)

Hi Aisha / Samir —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. HealthForge is a great fit for the pilot we discussed (patient summaries + embedding search for clinical notes). They asked for a more aggressive commercial structure to get procurement and the clinical team across the finish line before their Q4 budget window.

Proposal (one-time Q4 pilot):
- 3-month pilot, up to 500k tokens/month
- One-time structured rebate: 30% on pilot invoice, issued as a retrospective usage credit applied to first paid month post-pilot OR split into milestone credits (50/50 at month 2 & month 4)
- Standard enterprise SLA and SOC clauses apply (attached: Redwood-SLA-Q4.xlsx).

I want to be conservative with the concession but flexible enough to win this reference. Can we treat this as a one-time commercial rebate (not a permanent list-price discount) and document it as a rebate schedule in the term sheet? Attaching a short term-sheet stub: HF-req-rebate-term-sheet.pdf

Please confirm if this structure is acceptable and I will loop in procurement/legal to finalize.

Next step: Aisha/Samir — can you confirm internal approval timeline?

Best,
Michael
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: HF-req-rebate-term-sheet.pdf (term sheet stub), Redwood-SLA-Q4.xlsx (SLA summary)

Michael —

Thanks — the structure looks promising. Two asks from our side: 1) can HealthForge get a larger headline concession (they're asking for something closer to 40% on the pilot invoice); and 2) they'd prefer the credit to be distributed across a 6-month post-pilot period to make the economics smoother for their CFO.

Our procurement team wants the term sheet and a short note that this is a one-off concession tied to the pilot and reference outcomes. If you can provide that, we can fast-track legal review this week.

Aisha
Head of Partnerships, HealthForge

Team —

HealthForge pushed back and is asking for a 40% pilot rebate and to spread credits over 6 months. This is a strategic pilot (healthcare reference; potential ARR expansion) but also a material concession if we treat it as a cash-equivalent credit. Quick summary and options:

Context:
- Account: HealthForge (HF-98765) — want to start pilot in Oct, internal procurement timeline ~2 weeks
- Proposed pilot spend: ~$18k/month list (500k tokens/month estimate)
- Current ask: 40% one-time rebate, 6-month distribution

Options for approval (recommended language for execs):
A) Approve one-time rebate up to 30%, documented as retrospective usage credits applied to invoices over 3 months. Requires VP approval. No change to list price; rebate expires after pilot.
B) Approve up to 40% but only if rebate is milestone-based (release 50% after pilot success metrics met; remaining 50% after first paid month and reference commitment). Requires CFO sign-off and finance holdback documentation.
C) Decline deeper concession; offer starter credit (20%) + product support package and extended trial instead.

Attachments: HF-req-rebate-term-sheet.pdf, Redwood-SLA-Q4.xlsx.

Ask: @Lauren can you approve up to 30%? If >30% is needed, please route to Rafael/CFO with the proposal in Option B. 

Thanks — I can prepare the clause and update HubSpot (deal HF-98765) once we have direction.

-Michael

- Finance to confirm how rebate will be booked (capex vs. credit memo).

If team wants to go past 30% to 40%, escalate to Rafael for CFO-level sign-off. Rafael — please weigh in with a recommended concession ceiling and whether milestone-based distribution addresses your booking concerns.

Marissa / Michael: prepare a short exec memo (one pager) that I can forward to our CFO if needed. Include: commercial structure, expected dilution %, recovery mechanics, and reference commitment language.

Team —

Reviewed numbers and HS-forecast. I will approve a one-time rebate structure subject to the following guardrails:
1) Max rebate cap: 20% of the pilot invoice if credits are front-loaded or immediately applied as invoice credits.
2) Up to 30% allowed only if credits are milestone-based (50% after defined success metric; remaining 50% upon conversion to paid subscription) and legal adds an explicit clawback clause if HealthForge fails to convert.
3) All concessions must be logged in HubSpot (deal HF-98765) and require a note with accounting treatment; product must sign off on the success metrics.

So next steps for Sales: choose A (30% retrospective credits over 3 months) under Lauren's prior floor, or decide B (milestone structure) but be prepared to submit the exec memo for CFO sign-off. I will not sign off any headline rebate >30% without CFO visible approval.

Michael / Marissa — update the term-sheet with the milestone language (I flagged HF-req-rebate-term-sheet.pdf). Once updated, attach to HubSpot and ping me; I will route to finance ops for booking guidance.

-Rafael
